subject: Critical threshold escalation: Auratek throughput + error spike — exec briefing & customer update
messages:
From: Michael Chen <michael.chen@auratek.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <agomez@auratek.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: High error rate and throughput drop — immediate help needed

Priyom,

We started seeing a sharp increase in generation errors and a corresponding throughput collapse on our production integration at ~14:45 UTC. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~8% and tail latency spiked to multiple seconds for many short requests. This is impacting our checkout flow — already reported two customer incidents.

Attached is a small sample of the error responses and a short timeline from our side (auratek_error_log_20271101.json). Can you confirm if this aligns with any infra changes on Redwood? We’re on the dedicated plan (pool: auratek-dedicated-1). We need an ETA for a mitigation or rollback.

-Michael
Head of Engineering, Auratek
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@auratek.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@auratek.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: RE: High error rate and throughput drop — immediate help needed

Team — urgent. Auratek is reporting an 8% error rate+tail latency on their dedicated pool. They are in prod checkout; high customer impact.

Immediate asks:
- Vivek: can you spin up an emergency triage slot and check kernel/quantization routing, model variant fallbacks, and any autoscaler events for pool auratek-dedicated-1? Flag potential rollback to earlier model build if necessary.
- Marissa: draft a short customer note (acknowledgement + short-term mitigation plan) we can send in 30m. Keep tone calm and concrete.
- Lauren: loop in CS for an outreach cadence and check SLA credits policy (do we need to pre-authorize any credits)?

I’m going to put an exec-only brief together for Sarah/CTO and the CRO; if we need escalation beyond that we’ll pull them in. Mic, Alicia — we’ll update in 30/60/120 minute cadence.

---
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
priom@redwood.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@auratek.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 15:28:00 +0000
Subject: RE: High error rate and throughput drop — immediate help needed

On it — I’ve triaged the pool and see three correlated signals: a) a sudden kernel selector change that routed some requests to q8_fast on a subset of nodes, b) a spike in KV cache miss rates which increased compute per request, and c) autoscaler oscillation triggered by a higher-than-usual short-seq pattern.

Short-term mitigations (15–45m):
- Force roll routing back to q4_stable on affected nodes (will reduce max throughput but lower error rate).
- Disable aggressive autoscale burst for auratek-dedicated-1 to stop flapping; pin min nodes until stable.
- Apply a temporary prefix cache population for hot keys identified in their logs.

I’m launching the actions now. If the error rate doesn’t drop under 1% in 30m we’ll rollback the model build to v20271018. I’ll post telemetry screenshots once the rollback or routing change completes.

Attachments: auratek_error_log_20271101.json (excerpt)

—Vivek
Director, Serving Runtime
vivek@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chen <michael.chen@auratek.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@auratek.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Auratek — immediate update and next steps (short note)

Michael / Alicia —

Thank you for raising this. We’ve confirmed the issue on our side and have implemented initial mitigations to stabilize throughput and reduce the error rate. High-level status:

- What happened: routing and cache pressure caused a small segment of nodes to serve with an unstable kernel path; this produced elevated errors and increased tail latency.
- What we did (now): forced stable routing, pinned minimum capacity, and applied a hot-prefix cache seed.
- Near-term impact: we expect error rate to fall below 1% within 30 minutes and tail latency to return to baseline in 60 minutes.
- Follow-up: if we don’t meet these targets we will rollback to model build v20271018 and run a controlled canary.

We apologize for the disruption and will keep you updated at 30/60/120 minute marks. I’ve attached a one-slide summary for postmortem use (customer-impact-slide-v1.pdf).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chen <michael.chen@auratek.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@auratek.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Critical threshold escalation: Auratek throughput + error spike — exec briefing & customer update

Michael / Alicia — quick summary and next steps after our remediation window.

Status: stabilized. Error rate peaked at 8.1% at 14:46 UTC on 2027-11-01, dropped to 0.6% within 32 minutes after we forced route rollback and cache seeding. Tail latency returned to baseline within ~55 minutes. We did not need to perform a full model rollback.

Actions taken (closed):
- Forced kernel routing to q4_stable on affected nodes (15:25–15:30 UTC).
- Pinned autoscaler min nodes and paused burst policy (15:30 UTC).
- Populated hot-prefix cache and primed common keys (15:32–15:40 UTC).

Next steps (24–72h):
- Run a deeper postmortem to identify why kernel selector changed for this pool; expect report by EOD tomorrow.
- Follow-up canary: controlled test on v20271025 in our staging cluster + customer opt-in for a scheduled roll.
- Compensation: Lauren will follow up on SLA credits and any commercial remediation if requested.

We will send a final incident report (timeline, root cause, and prevention plan) once the postmortem is complete. Please let me know if you need an immediate phone bridge; we can schedule executive review if Auratek leadership requests it.

Thanks for your patience and for surfacing the logs — those made it much faster to isolate the chain.

-Priyom
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
priom@redwood.com
